title: Adjuvant paclitaxel and trastuzumab for small node-negative HER2-positive breast cancer: final 10-year analysis
journal: Lancet Oncology 2023; final 10-year analysis of the open-label, single-arm phase II APT trial
population: 410 enrolled; 406 initiated protocol therapy and were included in the treated analysis population. Small HER2-positive node-negative tumours ≤3 cm; median age 55 years; 67% HR-positive.
treatment: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly for 12 weeks with trastuzumab, followed by trastuzumab to complete one year.
summary: At median follow-up 10.8 years, 10-year iDFS was 91.3% (95% CI 88.3–94.4), recurrence-free interval 96.3% (95% CI 94.3–98.3), OS 94.3% (95% CI 91.8–96.8), and breast cancer-specific survival 98.8% (95% CI 97.6–100.0).

absoluteEffect.toxicity: Grade 3–4 neuropathy 4%, neutropenia 4%, transaminitis 3%; reversible symptomatic grade 3 LV systolic dysfunction 0.5%.

clinicalInterpretation: APT supports a less intensive adjuvant option for carefully selected small node-negative HER2-positive breast cancers, with excellent 10-year breast cancer-specific survival. Because the study was single-arm, it cannot establish comparative benefit or non-inferiority to more intensive chemotherapy.
criticalReview: The 10-year iDFS rate was 91.3%, while RFI was 96.3%; the distinction matters because iDFS includes contralateral breast cancers and deaths not necessarily attributable to the index tumour. 356/406 patients completed all 52 weeks; 24 stopped for protocol-specified toxicity and six for other toxicities. The trial does not justify extrapolation to larger, node-positive or otherwise high-risk HER2-positive cancers.
